codebook_ambiguities: Compound gold values whose alias list contains single components (F29 'computational linguistics'/'auditing', F01 '30 minutes'/'quarter to five', F22 'working'/'web based'): the matcher makes a two-or-more-content-word alias a strong match, but semantically one component is a fragment. The codebook does not say whether a component alias carries the whole value, so split_across_claims and alias-based carrying conflict. The round-1 audit treated fragments as wrong, and I followed that.

A gold value embedded as a presupposition in a claim about something else (F81: 'BLAS scores on the 3 [ORGANIZATION6] online ASRs' for the count 'three') is not covered: the text contains the whole value, but the claim asserts something else.

There is no sub-code for a fact holding the full value that is superseded by a partial restatement of the same gold value (F01: '30 minutes, actually 28 minutes' replaces '30 minutes ... quarter to 5'). overwritten_by_non_gold_value fits poorly, and whether 'current' passes depends on the fragment judgement.

Mixed carriers for compound values: the 'proposed' step accepts any proposal carrying the value, even when it comes from a claim that failed the modality step (F22: 'web based' came only from a proposed-modality claim, while the asserted 'pretty working' claim's proposals were for other values). The codebook does not say whether the proposal must carry the same part, or come from a carrier that passed polarity and modality.

In A1 runs each phase has two logged evaluations per claim (the regular pass, then the bug-13 settle pass). The codebook does not say explicitly that a proposal raised in the first pass and expired by the settle pass of the same phase counts as 'raised by k' (F37). I treated it as passing 'proposed' and failing 'applied' with proposal_expired.

Cited-span location is ambiguous for short gold lines such as 'PERSON3: Yeah, yeah.', which match many spans, and for evidence lines that fall in different spans (F22 lines 8-12 over two spans, F61 lines 344/356 over two spans, one evidence_only). The codebook does not say whether every such span is a cited span for locality, or how a short line is tied to one span.

displaced_by_other_gold_value says 'another gold value of the checkpoint', but not whether that value must belong to a row on the same gold key or to any row. In F02 the displacing fact holds F69 '18 April' (demo.deployment_deadline), misfiled on the SLT-deadline key. I counted any row's value.

Ruled-out records that hold the value's words: for F37, a REJECTED fact from a negative claim about one setup lacking launchers. The codebook excludes ruled-out records for current rows at 'applied', but it is silent on whether such a record should affect the sub-code choice (proposal_expired vs fact_not_found).

findings.title: Sibling rule: an equal share ignores locality, and complementary F/R pairs are treated as rivals
findings.location: 23-loss-trace.py Judge.level (lines 636-647); gold collisions F06/F38, F61/R04 (also F32/R02, F70/R05, F82/R06, F91/R08)
findings.claim: When a text contains a phrase that another row of the same checkpoint also contains, equally, v2 downgrades it to weak. It does this even when the text is local to this row and not to the other one, and even when the two rows are two sides of one decision with the same evidence line. On held-out A2, 4 of the 48 refusals or downgrades are wrong (2 claims), and the other 44 are right. Two cases are affected. (1) F06 '42 languages' and F38 'all 42 languages' share the aliases '42 languages' and '42'. F06's own local claim 'PERSON6 multilingual model | has | 42-language model' ('multilingual model for 42 languages' in r3 runs) passes carried at k=0 but becomes weak at k>=1, so F06 k1-3 is a carried loss in all 7 runs. This holds in the round-1-adjudicated primary series too (lt_r2.json: 21/21 rows carried:split_across_claims). (2) R04 and F61 share evidence line EL2020c:356 and the alias 'not to the test set'. 'put mainly to training data, not to the [PROJECT5] test set' becomes weak for R04, so R04 k2-3 is carried:claims_without_the_value in all 7 runs. In a1_r2 and a1_r3 the carrier is a NEGATIVE asserted claim ('not to use the [PROJECT5] test set; put this mainly to training data'), and R04 is actually stored: key_reached:other_keys_resolved at k2 and ok:stored_not_asked at k3.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: Measured with a scratch patch on all 7 runs: 35 rows change (F06 21, R04 14), 25 of them at the boundary. Held-out A2 alone: 5 rows, 3 at the boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: In Judge.level: (i) never treat as siblings two rows that share a gold evidence line (this covers all five F/R collision pairs); (ii) on an equal share, keep the match for the row the text is local to when it is not local to the other row. Pass a per-row local-set function through ctx. Tested in scratch: lt_sibling.py.

findings.title: Identity propagation from a claim that carries only through subject+predicate+object credits facts that do not hold the value
findings.location: trace_row carried_kv (line 695) and holds() (697-701), which feed proposed, applied, current, status and reading
findings.claim: carried_kv adds (key, object) for every carrier claim, including claims that matched only through their subject+predicate+object text. The stored proposal or fact keeps only the object, often under an unrelated key, and so loses the words that carried the value. Examples: R05 'not the only solution' under data_extraction.status (A0 r1) and under translation.strategy.considered (A1 r1); F21 'word-level alignment' (a1_r2); F68 'critical' under project.language.future_use (a1_r2); F22 'pretty well' under translation_output.language_mix (a1_r2); F53 'done now' (a0_r2); F39 'English' under document.translation*.language (A0 r1, a1_r2, a1_r3, A2 k1-3). These rows are credited as proposed, applied or stored, and the loss shows up at reading or not at all. Where the key does carry the subject, propagation is right: A2 R05 under ...tpu_only_solution_rejected, and F08 under pipeline.asr.assessment.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: Refined fix measured on 7 runs: 26 rows change, 19 at the boundary (A0 r1 3, A1 r1 2, A2 3 sub-code only, a1_r2 13, a0_r2 3, a1_r3 1). Requiring a strong match instead would also drop 15 F31 rows that are acceptable (fragment or true).
findings.suggested_fix: Propagate identity from a claim whose object did not count only when the key words plus the value ('a.b_c value' -> 'a b c value') match at least weakly, with the sibling rule applied (judge.level(keyed) is not None). Otherwise record applied:value_stored_without_subject. Tested in scratch: lt_spoid2.py.

findings.title: phrases() skips the covered part of a value once an alias is contained, so the one-word upgrade lets a sibling's text carry a numeric value
findings.location: phrases() line 244 ('and not out'); Judge.level one-word upgrade lines 644-646
findings.claim: For F82 the text 'average of the scores of the 3 ASRs and pick the best' contains the aliases 'average of the scores' and 'pick the best', so phrases() never adds F82's covered value words {average, score, 3, asr, pick, best}. F81's {3} is then 'free', its weak match is upgraded to strong (one-word value, local text), and F82's fact counts as F81's (judged X). In held-out A2, F81 k3 passes proposed and applied only on this X fact and reaches key_reached:other_keys_resolved. With the X removed it is filed:cycle2_parked_unsupported_by_span. a0_r2 has the same pattern.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 2 rows over 7 runs (A2 and a0_r2 F81 k3), both at the boundary. The fix changes exactly these 2 rows.
findings.suggested_fix: In phrases(), always add the covered part of the value when coverage >= 0.5, whether or not an alias is contained (remove 'not out'). Optionally limit the one-word upgrade to texts where no other row covers half its value. Tested in scratch: lt_phrases.py.

findings.title: Strict false positives never reach the adjudication queue, and adjudications are keyed by exact string, so an object-text decision misses the same claim's SPO text
findings.location: main() queue construction (lines 1065-1072); Judge.counts adj lookup (650); claim_counts (684-687)
findings.claim: The queue holds only texts whose lenient and strict outcomes differ, plus wording pairs. A strong local text that is wrong counts in both bounds and is never queued, for example F81's X in A2 and a0_r2. A decision is also matched on the exact string: claim_counts tries the object first, then the SPO text, so a 'false' on the object leaves the SPO path open. Evidence in the primary series (lt_r2.json with adj_round1.yaml): round 1 set F61 'organization of the test/training data not yet available' to false. In A1 r1 the SPO text 'test organization considered organization of the test/training data not yet available' still counts, so F61 k2 reaches answered:answer_or_judge and k3 ok:stored_not_asked. Adding the SPO variants as false moves both rows to proposed:another_value_won.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: In the adjudicated primary series over 7 runs: 4 rows at the boundary (A1 r1 F61 k2-3, A2 F81 k3, a0_r2 F81 k3).
findings.suggested_fix: Adjudicate claims, not strings: a decision on either a claim's object or its SPO text applies to that claim (and its identity propagation). Also queue every text that is the only support of a strict pass at proposed or applied, at least those reached through identity propagation or the one-word upgrade. That is at most 72-84 unique texts per run (72 in A2), so adjudicating all of them is feasible.

findings.title: split_across_claims mislabels sibling-rule refusals
findings.claim: The split test runs raw match_level, without the sibling rule, on the joined objects of local claims with the same subject. It does not check whether one claim already matches. For F06 k1-3, the single claim '42-language model' matches raw strong but the sibling rule refuses it. Joining it with '6-language model' then matches strong, so the row is labelled split_across_claims, although no value is split. F23 in A2 is a real split ('Czech ASR into other thing' / 'English ASR into all the things' / 'maybe French ASR') and stays correct.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 21 rows (F06 k1-3 in all 7 runs) labelled wrongly in raw strict and in the primary series; R04 k2-3 (14) gets the same new label under the fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the split test, if any local claim by k matches raw strong on its object or SPO but the judge refused it, return carried:sibling_value_only. Run the split test through Judge.level and include subjects in the joined text, so that the two 'Overleaf | created/empty' claims for F56 are seen together. Tested in scratch: lt_split.py.

findings.title: Stemmer leaves doubled consonants and inconsistent stems ('dropped' -> 'dropp' vs 'drop')
findings.claim: Doubled consonants survive the -ed/-ing strip: dropped/dropping -> 'dropp', stopped -> 'stopp', planned -> 'plann', submitted -> 'submitt'. Other pairs also stem differently: using/used vs use/uses, based -> 'bas' vs basis -> 'basi', goes -> 'goe'. In held-out A2, R06's negative asserted carrier 'Antrecorp | rejected | dropped from consideration because it is very unstable' misses the alias 'drop Antrecorp' and is only weak (through 'Antrecorp', shared with R03). Fixed together with the sibling exemption (F82 and R06 share EL2020d:22), R06 k3 moves from carried:claims_without_the_value to proposed:another_value_won. The stem fix alone changes 0 rows.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 1 boundary row in A2 (R06 k3), together with finding 1. Round 1 adjudicated only the text 'Antrecorp', which does not cover this SPO text.
findings.suggested_fix: After stripping -ed or -ing, undouble a final doubled consonant other than l, s or z. Map use/using/used and basis/based to a single stem.

findings.title: One-word or collapsing aliases stay weak even when they are the core of the value in a local text
findings.location: _match (weak one_word path, 208, 215, 220-221); Judge.level upgrade applies to one-word VALUES only; gold aliases
findings.claim: Some aliases are a single content word after stop words are removed: '23rd' (F67), 'send it to me' -> {send} (R01), 'the paper' -> {paper} (F56), 'the 3' -> {3} (F81). They stay weak in local texts. F67 'demo timing | decided | after the edible SLT, around the 23rd' is a true carrier, but raw strict gives carried:claims_without_the_value in A2 (k2-3); round 1 adjudicated it true. R01 'PERSON2 | will send | the document by tonight' is the rejected plan stated positively. R01 k0-3 should be polarity:carried_only_positive, not carried:claims_without_the_value; this holds in 6 of 7 runs of the primary series, because round 1 adjudicated only 'sending the update by tonight'.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: A2: 6 rows (F67 x2 at the boundary; R01 x4 sub-code). Primary series: R01 about 24 rows (sub-code only).
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the strong upgrade to free one-word aliases that are numbers, dates or proper nouns in local texts. Do not extend it to common words: 'working' would admit F22 false positives such as 'the cleanup/release setup work'. Add a gold lint for aliases that collapse to one content word, and give them longer forms ('around the 23rd', 'send it to me by tonight').

findings.title: Order-free containment and predicate tokens let bag-of-words matches through
findings.claim: Containment ignores word order and distance. In A2, F83's alias 'not subtitle' matches 'visualization of subtitles ... ASR files not ready for evaluation', which is strong and local and decided a proposed pass, although a true text was also present. 'simple script' matches 'script edits for simple processing adjustments' (F25/F58). Because the SPO text includes the predicate, 'owns' (stemmed to 'own') satisfies F31's aliases 'own ASR' and 'train our own'. That gives credit for the wrong reason ('PERSON4 owns English ASR training implementation'; 'PERSON8 owns training another PROJECT6-based ASR' is only a fragment). Generic two-word aliases also admit rival options: 'issue tracker' admits 'Bugzilla issue tracker' (A0 r1 F24 k1-3, already adjudicated false in round 1).
findings.estimated_rows_affected: No row changes in the three censused runs beyond those adjudicated in round 1; latent
findings.suggested_fix: Require alias tokens to fall within a window of the alias length plus 2, and require a negator to come before its next alias word within 2 tokens. Leave the predicate out of the SPO text (or do not stem 'owns'). Flag generic aliases ('issue tracker', 'cruise control', 'training data', 'project officer') in the collision lint.

findings.title: Codebook omissions: what 'local' means, SPO identity, and the number-word rule
findings.claim: (1) Locality is decided by string identity: a non-local claim or a fact whose text equals a local claim's object counts as local. (2) The codebook says a fact holding a carrier claim's value carries the value. It does not say that when the carrier matched only through its subject, the fact's text may not hold the value (finding 2). (3) 'one' in a value ('one shared paper' F56, 'one new subdirectory' F60, 'one section per language' F04) becomes a required digit unless an alias matches. This is latent; in A2 F56 is a fragment split over two Overleaf claims in any case. (4) The lenient bound's non-local strong texts are 83% wrong on held-out data (see measurements), which supports keeping them out of strict.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 0 directly
findings.suggested_fix: State the string-identity locality and the SPO-identity behaviour in the Matcher section. Exempt determiner 'one' (or numbers in values of 4 or more content words) from the required-number rule.

rows.explanation: Both sides agree on the data. Claim c8b69081 'PROJECT1 test set | includes | computational linguistics domain' is extracted in phase 1 from cited span EL2020b#10. The codebook does not settle this: the matcher rule says yes, while the Limits note on compound values and the round-1 fragment category say no.
